files.Title: Hephaestus.AffineForm
files.Summary: The normal form of a linear expression: constant + Σ coefficient · variable, with variables in a fixed order and no zero coefficients. Two linear expressions denote the same function exactly when their affine forms are equal, so x + y and y + x normalise to equal values even though the expressions themselves differ.

files.Title: Hephaestus.AffineForms
files.Summary: Arithmetic and analysis over and .

files.Title: Hephaestus.Anchoring
files.Summary: Building points out of plain values and quantities: start + dwell. These cannot be generic operators, because no operand is a and generic code does not know how a TDelta is added to a T; so each point type declares its own T + Quantity<TDelta> operators beside its projection, in terms of these.

files.Title: Hephaestus.BinaryVariable
files.Summary: A variable that is either 0 or 1. It is both a linear expression (its 0/1 value) and a boolean expression (true exactly when it is 1), so it can be summed and scaled as well as combined with &, | and !.

files.Title: Hephaestus.BooleanConstant
files.Summary: A fixed truth value.

files.Title: Hephaestus.BooleanOperators
files.Summary: Logical operators over . As with the linear operators, these only build data; normal forms are computed later, when a model is encoded for a solver.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Column
files.Summary: A variable as a MILP solver sees it: with native bounds. The bounds are those the problem's top-level constraints state outright (x <= 10), or the variable's intrinsic ones.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Comparison
files.Summary: A comparison between two linear expressions.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Conjunction
files.Summary: Holds exactly when both sides hold.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Constant
files.Summary: A fixed real number.

files.Title: Hephaestus.ContinuousVariable
files.Summary: A variable ranging over the real numbers.

files.Title: Hephaestus.DateTimeOffsetProjection
files.Summary: Date-times with offsets, measured in multiples of a unit since an origin.

files.Title: Hephaestus.DateTimeProjection
files.Summary: Date-times measured in multiples of a unit since an origin.

files.Title: Hephaestus.DeepRecursion
files.Summary: Expressions are as-written trees, so folding + or & over a long sequence makes a tree as deep as the sequence is long. Recursive passes stay natural by continuing on a fresh stack whenever the current one is nearly exhausted, instead of overflowing. Public so that solver backends which walk expressions themselves can do the same.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Disjunction
files.Summary: Holds exactly when at least one side holds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.EncodingOptions
files.Summary: Settings for lowering a problem to a .

files.Title: Hephaestus.Equivalence
files.Summary: Holds exactly when both sides have the same truth value.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Evaluation
files.Summary: Reads expressions off a solution. Any expression can be read, not just variables.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Feasible
files.Summary: A solution that satisfies the constraint but is not proven best, typically because a limit was reached.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Formatting
files.Summary: Renders expressions the way they were written, for logs, error messages and code review: (departureA + 120 <= departureB) | (departureB + 120 <= departureA).

files.Title: Hephaestus.GuardedRow
files.Summary: Expression <= 0 (or == 0) whenever every guard holds. With no guards the row holds unconditionally.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Gurobi.GurobiBackend
files.Summary: Solves problems with Gurobi through its own .NET interface. As an it turns every guarded row into a Gurobi indicator constraint, so that no big-M appears anywhere; as an it takes the classic formulation with derived big-M values.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Gurobi.GurobiSolver
files.Summary: Ready-made solvers backed by Gurobi.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Highs.HighsBackend
files.Summary: Solves mixed-integer linear programmes with HiGHS, through the wrapper its maintainers publish.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Highs.HighsSolver
files.Summary: Ready-made solvers backed by HiGHS.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IBooleanExpression
files.Summary: A truth-valued expression over linear comparisons and binary variables. The cases are , , , , , , and . Like linear expressions, boolean expressions are plain data kept exactly as written.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IIndicatorBackend
files.Summary: A solver with indicator or half-reified constraints: it takes rows guarded by literals as they stand, so nothing is relaxed with a big-M and no bounds are needed for the encoding.

files.Title: Hephaestus.ILinearExpression
files.Summary: A real-valued expression that is linear (strictly: affine) in its variables. The cases are , , and the records. Expressions are plain data, kept exactly as written; all interpretation (normalisation, bounds, encoding, evaluation) happens in later passes.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IMilpBackend
files.Summary: A solver for plain mixed-integer linear programmes.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IPointProjection<T, TDelta>
files.Summary: The projection of a type whose values are positions rather than amounts (date-times, not durations). Positions cannot be added or scaled, but the difference between two of them is an amount, of type TDelta.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IProblem
files.Summary: An optimisation problem: a single constraint, optionally with an objective. There is no list of constraints, because a list would only duplicate what & already means; conjoin a collection with AllOf(). The cases are , and .

files.Title: Hephaestus.IProjection<T>
files.Summary: How values of a domain type lie along the solver's number line: for example durations measured in seconds, or date-times measured in seconds since some origin. A projection must be affine and increasing (equal steps in T are equal steps in number, and later means larger). That is what lets expressions under different projections of the same type be combined: the conversion between any two is recovered from where they send zero and one. Implement projections as records, so that equal projections compare equal.

files.Title: Hephaestus.ISolveResult
files.Summary: The outcome of solving a problem. The cases are , , , and .

files.Title: Hephaestus.ISolver
files.Summary: Anything that can solve a problem. This is the seam along which solvers are swapped: a backend that understands boolean structure natively (such as an SMT solver) implements it directly, while MILP backends implement the much smaller and are wrapped in a .

files.Title: Hephaestus.IVariable
files.Summary: A decision variable: a name and a kind, nothing more. Variables are values, so two variables of the same kind and name are the same variable. Bounds are not part of a variable; they are ordinary constraints (0 <= x & x <= 10), which the encoder recognises and passes to the solver as native bounds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Implication
files.Summary: Holds unless the antecedent holds and the consequent does not.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IndicatorProblem
files.Summary: A problem with its logic encoded but no big-M in sight: bounded columns, a linear objective, and rows that are linear except for being guarded by literals. This is the natural input for solvers with indicator constraints (Gurobi) or half-reified constraints (CP-SAT), and the half-way point on the road to a .

files.Title: Hephaestus.IndicatorProblems
files.Summary: Functions over .

files.Title: Hephaestus.IndicatorSolver
files.Summary: Turns any indicator backend into a solver for full problems: encode the logic, solve, then hide the auxiliary variables and snap whole-number variables to whole numbers. No big-M is involved.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Infeasible
files.Summary: The constraint cannot be satisfied.

files.Title: Hephaestus.IntegerVariable
files.Summary: A variable ranging over the whole numbers.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Interval
files.Summary: A closed interval of real numbers; either end may be infinite.

files.Title: Hephaestus.LinearNormalisation
files.Summary: The pass that flattens an as-written linear expression into its .

files.Title: Hephaestus.LinearOperators
files.Summary: Arithmetic and comparison operators over . Operators only build data: a + b is new Sum(a, b), nothing is simplified or flattened here.

files.Title: Hephaestus.LinearRow
files.Summary: The linear constraint LowerBound <= Σ coefficient · variable <= UpperBound.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Literal
files.Summary: A binary variable, or its negation.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Maximisation
files.Summary: Find an assignment that makes the objective as large as possible while the constraint holds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.MilpEncoding
files.Summary: Lowers a problem in pure steps: normalise and encode the logic with guarded rows, giving an ; then propagate bounds and relax the guards with big-M values derived from them, giving a .

files.Title: Hephaestus.MilpProblem
files.Summary: A problem lowered to a plain mixed-integer linear programme: bounded columns, linear rows and a linear objective. This is all a MILP backend ever needs to understand.

files.Title: Hephaestus.MilpProblems
files.Summary: Functions over .

files.Title: Hephaestus.MilpSolver
files.Summary: Turns any MILP backend into a solver for full problems: encode, relax the guards with derived big-M values, solve, then hide the auxiliary variables and snap whole-number variables to whole numbers.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Minimisation
files.Summary: Find an assignment that makes the objective as small as possible while the constraint holds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.ModellingException
files.Summary: Thrown when a model cannot be given a meaning: clashing variable names, non-finite coefficients, or a big-M value that cannot be derived because a variable lacks bounds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Negation
files.Summary: Holds exactly when the operand does not.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.DayPeriodProjection
files.Summary: Periods measured in whole days. Only periods made of days and weeks have a fixed length, so only those can be encoded: a month is not a number of days.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.DurationProjection
files.Summary: Durations measured in multiples of a unit.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.InstantProjection
files.Summary: Instants measured in multiples of a unit since an origin.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.LocalDateProjection
files.Summary: Dates measured in whole days since an origin.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.LocalDateTimeProjection
files.Summary: Local date-times measured in multiples of a unit since an origin, along a local time line on which every day has twenty-four hours (as it has for a railway timetable within one zone).

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.LocalTimeProjection
files.Summary: Times of day measured in multiples of a unit since midnight. A time of day cannot leave its day, so constrain such variables to it (time.Between(LocalTime.Midnight, LocalTime.MaxValue)); numbers outside the day decode to its nearest end.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.NodaTimeOperators
files.Summary: A plain NodaTime value shifted by a quantity is a point whose origin is that value: start + dwell, dwell + start, start - dwell.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.NodaTimeVariables
files.Summary: Typed variables for the NodaTime types, offered alongside Variable.Continuous and friends. In every case unit is what the number one stands for (a second unless stated), and inWholeUnits makes the underlying variable an integer, for quantised times.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.OffsetDateTimeProjection
files.Summary: Offset date-times measured along the global time line; decoded values carry the origin's offset.

files.Title: Hephaestus.NodaTime.ZonedDateTimeProjection
files.Summary: Zoned date-times measured along the global time line; decoded values are in the origin's zone.

files.Title: Hephaestus.ObjectiveSense
files.Summary: Whether the objective of a is to be made small or large.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Occurrences
files.Summary: Finds the variables that expressions and problems mention.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Optimal
files.Summary: A solution that is proven to be the best possible.

files.Title: Hephaestus.OrTools.CpSatBackend
files.Summary: Solves whole-number problems with CP-SAT through its own interface. A guarded row becomes a linear constraint that is only enforced if its guards hold, which is CP-SAT's native idiom, so there is no big-M at all. CP-SAT reasons over finite whole-number domains: every variable must be an integer or binary, and must be bounded (directly or by implication).

files.Title: Hephaestus.OrTools.CpSatSolver
files.Summary: Ready-made CP-SAT solvers.

files.Title: Hephaestus.OrTools.OrToolsBackend
files.Summary: Solves mixed-integer linear programmes with a solver driven through Google OR-Tools.

files.Title: Hephaestus.OrTools.OrToolsSolver
files.Summary: Ready-made solvers backed by OR-Tools.

files.Title: Hephaestus.OrTools.OrToolsSolverId
files.Summary: The identifiers of solvers that OR-Tools can drive. Which are available depends on the OR-Tools build and on installed licences.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Point<T, TDelta>
files.Summary: A linear expression read as a position of type T: a date-time, a chainage. Points can be compared and shifted by quantities of TDelta, and the difference of two points is such a quantity; adding or scaling points does not type-check.

files.Title: Hephaestus.PointOperators
files.Summary: The algebra of positions: point - point is a quantity, point ± quantity is a point, and points compare with points. There is deliberately no point + point and no scaling.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Problem
files.Summary: Factory functions that read like the mathematics: Problem.Minimise(cost, subjectTo: constraint).

files.Title: Hephaestus.Product
files.Summary: A linear expression scaled by a fixed coefficient. There is deliberately no product of two expressions: non-linear terms are unrepresentable.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Quantity<T>
files.Summary: A linear expression read as an amount of type T: a duration, a length, a cost. Quantities can be added, subtracted, scaled and compared, with each other and with plain T values.

files.Title: Hephaestus.QuantityOperators
files.Summary: The algebra of amounts. Every operator reduces to the corresponding operator on the underlying linear expressions, after bringing the right-hand side into the left-hand side's projection.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Relation
files.Summary: How the two sides of a relate.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Satisfaction
files.Summary: Find any assignment under which the constraint holds.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Solution
files.Summary: An assignment of values to a problem's variables, as found by a solver.

files.Title: Hephaestus.SolveResults
files.Summary: Functions over solve results.

files.Title: Hephaestus.SolverOptions
files.Summary: Limits and tuning that apply to any solver.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Sum
files.Summary: The sum of two linear expressions.

files.Title: Hephaestus.SystemTimeOperators
files.Summary: A plain date-time shifted by a time-span quantity is a point whose origin is that date-time.

files.Title: Hephaestus.SystemTimeVariables
files.Summary: Typed variables for the time types of the base class library.

files.Title: Hephaestus.TimeSpanProjection
files.Summary: Time spans measured in multiples of a unit.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Unbounded
files.Summary: The objective can be improved without limit.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Unknown
files.Summary: The solver stopped without an answer.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Variable
files.Summary: Factory functions for decision variables. Integration packages extend this type with typed variables (for example Variable.Duration from the NodaTime package).

files.Title: Hephaestus.VariableOrder
files.Summary: The fixed order in which variables appear in normal forms: by name, then by kind.

files.Title: Hephaestus.Z3.Z3Solver
files.Summary: Solves problems with the Z3 SMT solver. Boolean structure is handed over as it stands, so there are no auxiliary variables, no big-M values and no need for bounds; arithmetic is exact and rational, so strict inequalities mean exactly what they say.
